newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Customs directive confers individual rights - court.
newsitem.headline: Customs directive confers individual rights - court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Tuesday that Italy's failure to enact the EU directive on customs debt exposes them to liability from individuals.

The court restated its position from earlier rulings that Council directive provisions which are unconditional and sufficiently precise create direct rights for individuals which may be asserted before national courts.

"A Community provision is unconditional where it sets forth an obligation which is not qualified by any condition, or subject, in its implementation or effects, to the taking of any measure either by the Community institutions or by the member states," the court said.
"Moreover, a provision is sufficiently precise to be relied on by an individual and applied by a national court where it sets out an obligation in unequivocal terms."
The court said individual rights under the customs debt directive still apply even when special import arrangments for young bulls, under Commission regulation, are infringed, as in the present case.

Three Italian agricultural undertakings, under import arrangements for fattening young male bovine animals, failed to follow Community guidelines precisely and the Italian government withheld import levies.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)
"Commission Regulation (EEC) Nos 612/77 and 1384/77 - Special import arrangements in respect of certain young bovine animals for fattening Council directive 79/623/EEC"
Reference from the Corte Suprema di Cassazione for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Cooperativa Agricola Zootecnica S. Antonio and Others

on the interpretation of Council directive 79/623/EEC of 25 June 1979 on the harmonization of provisions laid down by law, regulation or administrative action relating to customs debt (OJ 1979 L, p. 31) and Commission regulation (EEC) 612/77 of 24 March 1977 laying down rules for the application of the special import arrangements in respect of certain young male bovine animals for fattening (OJ 1977 L 77, p. 18), as amended by Community regulation (EEC) No 1384/77 of 27 June 1977 (OJ 1977 L 157, p. 16), and on the validity of Commission regulation (EEC) No 1121/87 of 23 April 1987 amending regulations (EEC) No 612/77 and No 1136/79 as regards the release of the security for certain special import arrangements in the beef and veal sector (OJ 1987 L 109, p. 12)

1. Article 2(d) of Council directive 79/623/EEC of 25 June 1979 on the harmonization of provisions laid down by law, regulation or administrative action relating to customs debt has direct effect and confers on individuals rights which they may assert against a member state which has failed to transpose the directive into national law, and which the national courts must safeguard.

2. Article 2(d) of directive 79/623/EEC is also applicable where Commission regulation (EEC) 612/77 of 24 March 1977 laying down rules for the application of the special import arrangements in respect of certain young male bovine animals for fattening as amended by Community regulation (EEC) No 1384/77 of 27 June 1977, is infringed.
